parsed.summary: The file proves two things. First, there is a finite connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H on Fin q, with a proper 2-colouring in which each colour class contains a vertex of degree ≥ 3, and constants c, ε > 0 such that c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n. Second, it proves the negation of Erdős's degeneracy conjecture: for all r > 0, every bipartite r-degenerate H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}). This matches Theorem 1.2 and is slightly stronger because of the extra max-degree condition. No significant faithfulness caveat was found; the main point to note is that degeneracy is phrased via induced vertex subsets, which is equivalent to the standard subgraph definition.

glossary.plain: N_G(v) ∩ s, the neighbours of v inside the finite set s
glossary.standard_concept: neighbourhood restricted to a vertex subset

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s contains a vertex with at most r neighbours inside s, i.e. every nonempty induced subgraph has minimum degree ≤ r
glossary.note: The paper phrases it via subgraphs. It is equivalent to the induced version, since deleting edges only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For all r > 0 and every bipartite r-degenerate finite graph H, ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) as n → ∞
glossary.note: r > 0 avoids the 1/0 junk value; extremalNumber is Mathlib's ex(n,H) on Fin n.

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q satisfying all of the following: H is connected; H is bipartite; H is 2-degenerate; some proper 2-colouring of H has, in each colour class, maximum degree > 2; and there are c, ε > 0 such that c·n^{3/2+ε} ≤ ex(n,H) for all sufficiently large n.
It is not the case that for every r > 0 and every bipartite r-degenerate finite graph H, ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
Erdős's conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate H has ex(n,H) = O(n^{2−1/r}) is false (already for r = 2).
Failure of the compactness conjecture (covered elsewhere, sibling file).

coverage.why: Same claim plus an extra condition: each bipartition class has maximum degree ≥ 3.
Negation of a faithful formalization of conjecture (3).

flags.explanation: The extra clause requires, for some proper 2-colouring, a vertex of degree > 2 in each colour class. This rules out the Füredi/AKS known case. It goes beyond the paper's stated theorem but only strengthens the Lean claim.

lint_verdicts.why: Finset.card of a filtered finset is a genuine count; there are no infinite types or junk values here.
The hypothesis 0 < r guarantees 1/(r:ℝ) is a genuine reciprocal.
(3:ℝ)/2 is real division and equals 1.5, with no truncation.
